records.name: Exceed Marketing Solutions
keyPersonnel: David P. Bolthouse (founder and CEO; manager in Florida's corporate register)
Barbro M. Bolthouse (manager in Florida's corporate register)
otherServices: Manages clients' "ancillary sites, social media, directory listings, hosting and email accounts"
"Search Ranking and AI Inclusion (SEO and GEO)"
records.notes: Describes itself as "a leading marketing partner for boarding schools and adolescent therapeutic programs, helping them achieve and maintain full enrollment," and tells programs that "participation with Exceed includes free featured listings in our highly ranked directories." Its directories tell parents their owners have "no ownership, investment, equity interest, or controlling interest in any program featured or listed." On October 2, 2026, 15 of the 16 program and directory websites that publish instructions for AI chatbots (llms.txt) were made with Exceed's software; the programs listed above are the ones whose websites were. A former director of Brush Creek Academy and New Lifehouse Academy gives a testimonial on Exceed's site. Exceed's website, the Best Choice Admissions sites and Exceed's directories share one Bing webmaster verification code.

records.name: Best Choice Admissions Services
keyPersonnel: David Bolthouse (chief executive, as The Warren reported in 2022)
otherServices: The help line on Exceed Marketing Solutions' directories; TeenChallengeSchools.com labels its pages "by Best Choice Admissions"
records.notes: Its home page says that "BEST CHOICE IS SPONSORED BY SCHOOLS AND PROGRAMS, THEREFORE OUR HELP IS OFFERED AT NO CHARGE TO FAMILIES." It shares a Spanish-language phone number with the Exceed directories. Earlier it told parents it was "a contracted agent of institutions" paid "a flat fee" for every enrollment; today it says it does not favor programs "based on financial incentives."

records.name: The Envoy Group
keyPersonnel: David Bolthouse (founder, as The Warren reported)
otherServices: A referral network: programs passed on parents' inquiries that were "not a good fit for your program (usually 90% or more aren't)" to other network programs
records.notes: Its pitch to programs: "easily referring inquiries that are not a good fit for your program (usually 90% or more aren't) with other network programs, and offset marketing costs while doing so," and "We custom target leads based on what parents are already searching for." Its site now says it "has closed its doors."

records.name: All Kinds of Therapy
keyPersonnel: Jenney Wilder (founder; closed her educational consulting practice in 2015)
otherServices: Directory listings for programs at $400 a month
records.notes: Its listing pages say "No pay-to-rank listings. Everyone here is human-verified." A 2026 press release calls it "a leading consumer-advocacy platform." Its listing for Provo Canyon School still called it "a leading national provider of residential youth treatment" after Utah ordered the school's last campus closed in July 2026.

keyPersonnel: Narvin Lichfield (founder; brother of Teen Help's founder, Bob Lichfield, per Salon, 1998)
otherServices: Sold schools a place in its directory for parents of "teens in crisis", with what it called "an exclusive technology that ensures top listing of ASI on most major search engines"
lawsuits: Wood v. World Wide Association of Specialty Programs, D. Utah No. 2:06-cv-708, Dkt. 282, Sept 16, 2008 (a 1999 Carolina Springs enrollment addendum)
company.notes: Salon reported in January 1998 that Adolescent Services was "founded last year by a man named Narvin Lichfield", that it and Teen Help "marketed a single set of closely affiliated schools", and that hundreds of near-identical copies of its pages filled search results, all recommending the same few schools. In Wood v. WWASP (D. Utah), a 1999 Carolina Springs enrollment addendum says ASI does not own or control the programs and offers a free month of tuition for referrals (Dkt. 282, Sept 16, 2008).
sourceUrls: Wood v. World Wide Association of Specialty Programs, D. Utah No. 2:06-cv-708, Dkt. 282 (Sept 16, 2008)

fills.name: Teen Revitalization

otherServices: An online directory of "twenty or more" programs with costs, a free child assessment and a loan application (its July 2006 press release)
company.notes:
Heavy.com reported on February 13, 2016 that "On the website Teen Revitalization, which advertises Midwest Academy, month-to-month rates are $3,490", adding that the site did not name Midwest but a school newsletter listed it among its schools. A printout of that article was e-filed in Lee County, Iowa district court on February 16, 2016, as part of Exhibit B in the Des Moines Register's case for the sealed Midwest Academy search warrants (Nos. SWSW000569 and SWSW000570).

Its own press releases call it "an organization that consists of a group of premier hand-selected boarding schools" (PRLeap, August 10, 2006) and say "Twenty or more troubled youth programs and schools are in the directory" (PR.com, July 26, 2006). Neither says how it was paid or whether the listed schools own it.

fills.name: Teens In Crisis

lawsuits: Wood v. World Wide Association of Specialty Programs and Schools, D. Utah No. 2:06-cv-00708 (dismissed as to Teens In Crisis, Apr 2007)
company.notes: Teens In Crisis, LLC was a named defendant in Wood v. WWASP (D. Utah No. 2:06-cv-00708). In April 2007 Judge Ted Stewart granted its motion to dismiss, finding the plaintiffs "failed to plead any fraudulent conduct with particularity as to Teens in Crisis"; in its motion it said it "had not received any commission for the enrollment of any plaintiff" (Memorandum Decision and Order, Docket No. 166).

dropNotes: Not yet sourced: it is named as a party in Wood v. WWASP (D. Utah) only in an advocacy group's 2006 press releases. The court docket has not been checked, so nothing here is confirmed.

keyPersonnel: Lon Woodbury (founder, 1989; stepped back from the website in 2017)
Ron and Kristie Campbell (owners of StrugglingTeens, LLC)
otherServices: Publishes programs' paid articles labeled "Paid Advertisement"
company.notes: Its own site says Lon Woodbury founded Woodbury Reports, "an educational consulting firm in North Idaho", in 1989, that StrugglingTeens.com "went live in 1995", and that in 2017 "the second generation took over". The same page, labeled "Paid Advertisement", names Ron and Kristie Campbell as owners of StrugglingTeens, LLC and invites programs to advertise (January 29, 2020).

otherServices: Charges programs per enrollment: "A set fee is charged only per student we bring you that you agree to enroll."
Its own advertising network for leads: "Our advertising network captures a steady flow of leads."
affiliations: Exceed Marketing Solutions: its page for programs carries an image named site-managed-by-exceed-small.png
company.notes: A referral and lead-generation service paid by programs, not a company that builds programs' websites. It tells families it is a "Free placement advisory / referral service - not a treatment provider" and that "we are compensated by participating schools"; its page for programs offers them students for a fee per enrollment. Its help email is the help line on Exceed Marketing Solutions' directory therapeuticboardingschools.org.

Vive Adolescent Care's ai.txt names webmaster@exceedmarketingsolutions.com as its contact (November 2026). Sunset Bay Academy and Oklahoma Adult and Teen Challenge carry files "Generated by Exceed LLMS plugin", but their ai.txt files name other contacts (conversiones.com and nicedigitals.com), so they are not listed as its clients.
